description:
Redwood Inference will produce and validate per-GPU “known good” runtime configurations (tuning profiles) for NVIDIA A100, H100, and B200 to make latency/throughput stable and repeatable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Goals:
- Define a small, curated set of supported runtime tuning profiles per GPU SKU (and common variants like SXM vs PCIe / MIG where applicable) that are performance-competitive but prioritize stability (low variance, predictable p95/p99).
- Reduce performance regressions and “mystery variance” by codifying kernel-selection, batching/scheduling parameters, memory/KV-cache settings, and compilation flags into versioned profiles.
- Establish a repeatable validation and release process: perf canaries + benchmark harness runs + regression thresholds + rollback procedure.
- Publish internal standards and operational guidance so SRE/Release Eng/Support can confidently roll profiles forward/back.

Scope:
- Runtime configuration surface: scheduler knobs (continuous batching, queue limits, prefill/decode split), KV cache settings (paging/compaction thresholds), kernel auto-selection constraints, quantization compatibility flags, and hardware-specific guardrails.
- Benchmarking: representative prompt-length distributions and concurrency mixes, plus a small set of “golden” workloads used as release gates.
- Release packaging: versioned profile artifacts, documented default selection logic by GPU, and an override mechanism for Dedicated/Private customers.

Non-goals:
- Building a new inference engine or rewriting kernels; work focuses on tuning and safe constraints around existing runtime capabilities.
- Customer-facing marketing collateral; this is primarily internal reliability/performance work (though it may feed release notes).

Stakeholders and roles:
- Runtime org (Mateo Alvarez, Hiro Tanaka, Sofia Ivanova; engineers like Grace Kim, Yuki Sato, Omar El-Sayed) owns implementation, kernel constraints, and scheduler changes.
- Applied ML / Performance & Evals (Jonas Weber, Arjun Desai, Claire Dubois) owns benchmark methodology, statistical validation, and regression gates.
- SRE/Observability (Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant) defines SLO-aligned thresholds, dashboards, and operational rollout checks.
- Release Engineering (Connor O’Brien) coordinates profile versioning, release trains, and change management.
- Program management (Talia Benson) runs cross-team execution and timeline.

Timeline (typical):
- Phase 0 (1–2 weeks): baseline collection + define profile schema and validation metrics.
- Phase 1 (2–4 weeks): A100 and H100 profiles + CI/perf canary gating.
- Phase 2 (2–4 weeks): B200 bring-up + additional safety constraints for new kernels/driver combos.
- Phase 3 (ongoing): iterative improvements, incident-driven hotfix profiles, and expansion to more model families/workloads.

Key deliverables:
- Versioned tuning profile artifacts for A100/H100/B200, with explicit defaults and override behavior.
- Benchmark suite updates and automated validation runs.
- Confluence docs: spec/ADR, performance standards, operational runbooks, and release notes.
- A small set of PRs across the runtime repo and benchmarking tooling to land the profile system and gates.

Constraints/risks:
- Hardware/driver/CUDA version variability across regions and deployment modes.
- Tail-latency sensitivity to small config changes; requires statistically robust gating.
- Need for rapid rollback and clear ownership during incidents or customer escalations.

files.description: High-level overview of the tuning profiles program: why stability matters, target GPUs (A100/H100/B200), supported workloads, success metrics (variance, p95/p99), and ownership.
Design spec for the profile schema (fields/knobs), how the runtime selects defaults based on GPU/driver/runtime version, and how overrides work for Dedicated/Private.
Formal standard defining pass/fail thresholds for a profile release (latency variance, throughput deltas, error rates), statistical methodology, and required benchmark coverage.
ADR recording the decision to version tuning profiles separately from the runtime, including alternatives considered (hard-coded defaults, per-model-only tuning) and rationale.
Step-by-step profiling guide for A100: tools, commands, expected traces, and common pitfalls (KV-cache pressure, kernel mismatch) for repeatable measurements.
Step-by-step profiling guide for H100, including notes on newer kernel paths, driver/CUDA constraints, and stability gotchas.
Bring-up checklist for B200: minimal viable config, validation order, and guardrails when enabling new kernels or compilation features.
Dashboards and alert definitions that gate profile promotion: which metrics to watch, anomaly detection, and escalation policy during rollouts.
Operational runbook for rolling back a tuning profile in hosted/dedicated/private contexts, including verification steps and communication templates.
Internal release notes summarizing the first A100/H100 profile set, expected performance impact, known limitations, and upgrade/rollback notes.
Internal release notes for initial B200 profile, including conservative defaults, validation status, and follow-up work.
Definition of the “golden” workload set (prompt distributions, concurrency mixes, model families) and why each is included for gating.
How to triage regressions attributed to profile changes: bisect strategy, which metrics isolate scheduler vs kernel vs memory, and when to hotfix.
Matrix of GPU SKUs (A100/H100/B200), instance types/regions, and approved driver/CUDA baselines used for profile validation.

Spreadsheet with baseline benchmark results (latency percentiles, throughput, variance) across A100/H100 before profile changes; includes notes on environments.
Export of parameter sweep results for A100 (batching limits, KV settings, kernel constraints) with tags for candidate profiles.
Export of parameter sweep results for H100; includes notes on instability cases and driver/CUDA interactions.
